items.title: Jack Teagarden Interview, 1959-10-29
items.q: But there was a band over at the Washington Hotel called, uh, the Louisiana Ramblers, Tim Kelly

ctx.x: And who was with you after that?

Oh, Terry Shand and, uh, and, uh, let's see. Terry, Terry Shand and I, we came and joined another band there, and it was called Youngberg Marin. It was about a nine or ten piece band. It was hotel work. But there was a band over at the Washington Hotel called, uh, the Louisiana Ramblers, Tim Kelly, and, uh, some, he's still in Louisiana, or Mississippi, Jackson, Mississippi, I think. And, uh, Pat and Bobby Dequeer, the boys, one played trumpet and one trombone, they were very good. But they weren't from…
Let's see. Uh, hold on. I hate to get started on anything. We'll just let it run off, huh, Paul? Yeah. I don't know. I don't know. I don't know.

items.title: Tim Kelly Interview, 1978-12-03
items.q: first time Jack Teagarden played in Shreveport, he played for Jasper Tompkins. Played with Terry Sheehan and Reginald Gullick.

ctx.x: We're talking about the number two band. Yeah.

So, uh. Ham sent us to Lake Charles, which is where I heard some early little bands we used to play. Big Lake and we played Shaw Beach, Pleasure Field. At that time, it was a real nice resort out in the lake. That was before Lake Charles became the Dakota Port. And, we were swimming and then we had a ballroom out over the world. And, it was real nice. We're talking about 1923 now. And, um. So, after leaving Lake Charles, this group of fellas, Brooks Prud and Dick Coleman and Buddy Seabee and myself, went back to…
